questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a. It regulates the operation of all body organs and protects the body and mind from becoming unbalanced as a result of negative circumstances and unhealthy lifestyles. b. It only requires frequent practice of the proper body motions and breathing techniques. c. The physical benefits of yoga can be enjoyed for a lifetime without risk or injury. d. It regulates the relationship between the body, the intellect, and the spirit.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct
logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
a. It regulates the operation of all body organs and protects the body and mind from becoming unbalanced as a result of
negative circumstances and unhealthy lifestyles.
b. It only requires frequent practice of the proper body motions and breathing techniques.
c. The physical benefits of yoga can be enjoyed for a lifetime without risk or injury.
d. It regulates the relationship between the body, the intellect, and the spirit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (2) i.e. c, b, d, a
 
Key Points
  • The sentence starts with "The physical benefits of yoga can be enjoyed for a lifetime without risk or injury," which is correctly indicated by part (c).
  • Following the introduction, "It only requires frequent practice of the proper body motions and breathing techniques" (b) continues the logical sequence, explaining the requirement for achieving those benefits.
  • The next part, "It regulates the relationship between the body, the intellect, and the spirit," elaborates on the benefits mentioned, indicated by (d).
  • Ending with, "It regulates the operation of all body organs and protects the body and mind from becoming unbalanced as a result of negative circumstances and unhealthy lifestyles" (a) completes the explanation by describing the holistic impact of yoga.
Therefore, the correct answer is c, b, d, a.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (d, a, b, c): This option disrupts the logical flow, starting with a general statement about regulation and ending with the benefits of yoga, which is less coherent.
  • Option 3 (b, a, c, d): This option places the requirement of practice before mentioning the benefits, making the initial statement unclear.
  • Option 4 (a, b, c, d): This option starts with a detailed function of yoga instead of introducing the benefits first, which is less effective for understanding the overall advantages.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. At times, David behaves in a very obdurate manner to kids.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word.
At times, David behaves in a very obdurate manner to kids.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "obdurate" means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action. (जिद्दी)
    • Example: Despite the pleas from his friends, he remained obdurate in his decision to leave the city.
  • "Obstinate" also means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or action, often despite attempts to persuade one to do so. (हठी)
    • Example: He was too obstinate to admit that he was wrong.
  • Hence, we can infer that "obdurate" is synonymous with "obstinate".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Trusting (विश्वास करने वाला): Showing or tending to have a belief in a person's honesty or sincerity; not suspicious.
    • Example: She was so trusting that she lent him her car without hesitation.
  • Amiable (मिलनसार): Having or displaying a friendly and pleasant manner.
    • Example: He was an amiable host, making everyone feel at home.
  • Envious (ईर्ष्यालु): Feeling or showing envy; wanting what someone else has.
    • Example: She was envious of her friend's new job.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Rahul won the extempore competition. He is lucky to be blessed with the gift of the gab .

The correct answer is: Option 4.

  • The idiom "gift of the gab" means a talent for speaking fluently and persuasively. (अच्छी और प्रभावशाली बातचीत करने की प्रतिभा)

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Nina has not yet learned how to straighten up and fly right .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Nina has not yet learned how to straighten up and fly right.

options.text: forget the wrongdoings of the others
options.html: forget the wrongdoings of the others

options.text: improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously
options.html: improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously

options.text: be professional in flying the aircraft
options.html: be professional in flying the aircraft

options.text: remember the past and prepare for the future
options.html: remember the past and prepare for the future

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "straighten up and fly right" is an idiomatic expression meaning to improve one's behavior, act properly, and conduct oneself correctly.
  • It does not refer to piloting an aircraft or addressing the past, rather it focuses on correcting one's improper behavior and becoming more responsible.
  • Thus, the most appropriate substitution is improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "Nina has not yet learned how to improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "forget the wrongdoings of the others" – This does not capture the meaning of improving one's own behavior.
  • Option 3: "be professional in flying the aircraft" – This is a literal interpretation involving aviation, which is unrelated to the idiomatic context of the sentence.
  • Option 4: "remember the past and prepare for the future" – This is about reflecting on the past and planning ahead, which, although good advice, does not convey the essence of improving inappropriate behavior.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I had not only helped her by giving hints but also with providing her links.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
I had not only helped her by giving hints but also with providing her links.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "not only... but also" is used to connect two related actions, emphasizing that both actions were done.
  • The correct format for this phrase in the sentence is: "helped her not only by giving hints but also by providing her links."
  • Thus, the most appropriate substitution is helped her not only by.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "I had helped her not only by giving hints but also by providing her links."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "helped her not by" – This changes the intended meaning of the sentence and does not use the "not only... but also" structure correctly.
  • Option 3: "helped her only by" – This implies that helping was limited to one action and does not reflect the intended emphasis of doing more than one thing.
  • Option 4: "helped not only her by" – This is incorrect because it disrupts the proper structure and meaning of the phrase "not only... but also."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Positive self-talk have a great affect on one’s self-worth.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Positive self-talk have a great affect on one’s self-worth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The verb "have" should be "has" to agree with the singular subject "Positive self-talk."
  • The correct noun is "effect" rather than "affect." "Effect" is the noun form that means a change that results from an action, whereas "affect" is usually a verb.
  • Thus, the correct substitution is has a great effect.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "Positive self-talk has a great effect on one’s self-worth."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "has a great affect" – The word "affect" is incorrect here; "effect" is needed.
  • Option 2: "have a great effect" – The verb "have" does not agree with the singular subject "Positive self-talk."
  • Option 3: "having a great affect" – The structure "having" and the word "affect" are both incorrect in this context.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Deepak is studying B.tech. at IIT Delhi to become the engineer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.

  • Option 3: "to become" – This part is correct; it accurately describes the purpose of his studies.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. He was given a reward for his contribution by the Governor.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
He was given a reward for his contribution by the Governor.

options.text: For his contribution, he was rewarded by the governor.
options.html: For his contribution, he was rewarded by the governor.

options.text: The governor gave him a reward for his contribution.
options.html: The governor gave him a reward for his contribution.

options.text: Rewarded by the governor, as he contributed along.
options.html: Rewarded by the governor, as he contributed along.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "The governor gave him a reward for his contribution."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a reward" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "gave" to "was given" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the governor."
  • Ensure the phrase "for his contribution" remains for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "The governor gave him a reward for his contribution."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "For his contribution, he was rewarded by the governor." – This is a passive voice sentence.
  • Option 2: "The governor rewarded him." – This is a correct active voice sentence but less detailed.
  • Option 4: "Rewarded by the governor, as he contributed along." – This is an incomplete and incorrect sentence structure.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Dealing with things in a practical and sensible way
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Dealing with things in a practical and sensible way
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "Pragmatic" means dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations. (व्यावहारिक)
    • Example: His pragmatic approach to problem-solving has always been effective.
  • "Pragmatic" refers to being practical and focused on reaching a goal. (व्यावहारिक)
    • Example: She took a pragmatic stance on the issue, favoring practical solutions over theoretical debates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

    • Example: His cynical view of the world made it difficult for him to trust others.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Foment
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Foment
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Regulate.

Key Points

  • The word "foment" means to instigate or stir up an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action. (उकसाना)
    • Example: He was accused of fomenting violence during the protests.
  • "Regulate" means to control or maintain the rate or speed of a machine or process so that it operates properly. (नियंत्रित करना)
    • Example: The government plans to regulate the financial market to prevent fraud.
  • Hence, the antonym of 'foment' is 'regulate'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Regulate.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Proximity (निकटता): Nearness in space, time, or relationship.
    • Example: The proximity of the school to my house is very convenient.
  • Remoteness (दूरस्थता): The state of being distant from something else, in particular from the main centers of population.
    • Example: The remoteness of the village makes it difficult to access healthcare.
  • Separation (विच्छेद): The action or state of moving or being moved apart.
    • Example: The separation of the two departments has led to better efficiency.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Sharat is always ______ about showing up for work because he believes that tardiness gets us nowhere.

  • The word "punctual" means happening or doing something at the agreed or proper time; on time. (समय पर)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Sachin Tendulkar was an indispensable member of the Indian cricket team in his days.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

Sachin Tendulkar was an indispensable member of the Indian cricket team in his days.
questions.solution:

  • "Essential" refers to something that is absolutely necessary; extremely important. (आवश्यक)
    • Example: Food, water, and shelter are essential for survival.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Essential.

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Motivational (प्रेरणादायक): Providing inspiration or encouragement.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'to'.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "according to" is a standard expression used to indicate that something is in agreement with or follows specific guidelines or rules.
  • In this context, the dance is created or choreographed and performed following the principles set out in the Natya Shastra.
  • The other options ("for", "of", "with") do not fit correctly in this phrase and do not convey the intended meaning.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.
 
Complete Passage: A dance which is created or choreographed and performed according (1) to the tenets of the Natya Shastra is called a classical dance. The two broad (2) categories of classical dancing are the tandava and the lasya. Power and force are typical of the tandava; grace and delicacy of the lasya. Tandava is (3) associated with Shiva, and lasya with Parvati. Dance which is pure movement is called nritta, and dance which is (4) expressive in nature is called nritya. A dancer, in the classical tradition, has to have years of training before he or she can begin to perform on the stage. The four main (5) forms of classical dancing in India are : Bharat Natyam, Kathakali, Manipuri, Kathak. Bharat Natyam is the oldest and most popular dance-form of India.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2 ("for") would indicate purpose or function, which is not suitable in this context.
  • Option 3 ("of") would indicate possession or belonging, which does not make sense here.
  • Option 4 ("with") would suggest accompaniment, which is not appropriate in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'aspects'.
 
Key Points
  • The context of the passage discusses the characteristics or features of classical dancing, specifically differentiating between tandava and lasya.
  • "Aspects" is the most fitting word as it refers to different parts or features of something, which aligns well with the discussion of the broad categories of classical dancing.
